rated_messages.input_message: When running a marathon, the hardest part is often towards the end, but many runners stick with it, knowing that the pain will pass. Learning to quit smoking is like running a marathon - if it gets hard, you may be closer to succeeding than you realize!
Craving a cig? Plan a fun activity you can do when you get home as a reward for not smoking.

Don't let anyone tell you how you should or shouldn't feel today. You feel how you feel and that's it. If you're happy and grateful then enjoy the moment, if you're angry and frustrated, know that this will pass.
Some people find that having a simple mantra can really help, especially if things feel stressful. Try repeating something simple to yourself like: "I can do it!".
Instead of lighting up a cigarette, light a scented candle or burn some incense.
Stress is temporary. It comes and goes like passing clouds in the sky. When stress demands you to light up, remember you can let it pass by without smoking.

Imagine that your urge is a backseat passenger trying to distract you from reaching your destination. See if you can choose to keep driving instead of allowing your urges to distract you from where you want to go.
Try chewing gum if you have trouble resisting smoking when other people light up around you.
Try to stop smoking by setting yourself a rule. For example, "IF I am tempted, THEN I will chew on some mints" - make your own rule that will work for you.
When a craving hits, keep your hands busy by doing the dishes or taking out the trash. Small chores will help pass the time during a craving.
